title: Women and the Revolution
objective: After this level you can describe the parts women played, from boycotts and camp work to Abigail Adams asking her husband to "remember the ladies".
summary: Women boycotted and spun homespun, followed the armies, and sometimes fought; Abigail Adams asked the lawmakers to "remember the ladies".

cards.headline: The Revolution was fought at spinning wheels and campfires too.
cards.body: Women boycotted, cooked, nursed and sometimes fought. One asked the men writing the new laws a pointed question.

cards.headline: Spinning as protest
cards.body: During the Stamp Act crisis, women formed the Daughters of Liberty. They gave up tea and gathered for spinning bees, making homespun cloth so their families didn’t need British imports. A boycott only works if someone makes the substitute.

cards.headline: Following the army
cards.body: Thousands of women, often soldiers’ wives, daughters or mothers, traveled with the armies as camp followers. They cooked, washed, sewed and nursed the sick and wounded. An army marches on clean shirts too.

cards.headline: In uniform
cards.body: A few women fought. In 1782 Deborah Sampson disguised herself as a man and enlisted in the 4th Massachusetts Regiment. Her secret held until she fell ill and a doctor discovered it.

cards.headline: Remember the ladies
cards.body: In March 1776 Abigail Adams wrote to her husband John in Congress: “I desire you would Remember the Ladies.” Women, she warned, would not feel bound by laws “in which we have no voice, or Representation.” It was the colonists’ own argument, turned on the men making it.

cards.headline: A brief vote
cards.body: One state went further, for a while. New Jersey’s 1776 constitution let property-holding inhabitants vote, and unmarried women and widows who qualified did. An 1807 law limited voting to free white men.

cards.headline: Women and the Revolution: explained
learned: The Daughters of Liberty spun homespun to boycott
Camp followers cooked, washed and nursed
Abigail Adams asked Congress to “Remember the Ladies”

questions.prompt: Match each woman or group with how they served the Revolution.
questions.explanation: The Daughters of Liberty held spinning bees, camp followers nursed the sick and wounded, Deborah Sampson enlisted in the 4th Massachusetts Regiment, and Abigail Adams wrote “Remember the Ladies.”

questions.prompt: How did spinning bees support the boycott of British goods?

options.label: They raised money to help colonists pay the British taxes
Homespun cloth replaced imported British cloth
They sold tea to the East India Company

questions.explanation: Women made homespun cloth so families could do without British imports.

questions.prompt: Abigail Adams objected to laws made with “no voice, or Representation” for women. Which earlier protest used the same logic?

options.label: The colonists’ protest against the Stamp Act
The Haudenosaunee founding of the Great Law of Peace
options.rationale: That was a Native constitution, not a protest about representation.

options.label: The Pueblo Revolt of 1680
options.rationale: That was a revolt against Spanish rule.

questions.explanation: Stamp Act protesters said they could be taxed only through their own representatives.
